title: 40 Years Ago, Oceanographers Found the Wreckage of the RMS Titanic - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistory40 Years Ago, Oceanographers Found the Wreckage of the RMS TitanicThe maritime disaster of 1912 wasn’t fully understood until the shipwreck was rediscoveredDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CDT on September 3, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThis week in 1985, oceanographers Jean-Louis Michel and Robert Ballard made a discovery of untold cultural impact: the wreckage of ill-fated oceanliner RMS Titanic. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoThe pair found the ship some 73 years after it collided with an iceberg and sank to the bottom of the Atlantic. The wreckage ended up around 12,500 feet under the surface, about 370 miles from the coast of Canada.Finding the long-lost ship wasn’t a simple task. For one, sonar scanning didn’t work, so Michel and Ballard decided instead to look for the debris that had spilled out of the Titanic, guessing (correctly) that this would cover a much wider area than the actual wreck. After a week of seeing nothing, the Titanic’s boiler was spotted on September 1st, and the researchers followed the debris trail back to the ship.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
